# truefoundry_role (Resource)

Manages a custom TrueFoundry role (`role` manifest) — a named set of permissions that `role_id` references such as a `truefoundry_ml_repo` collaborator resolve against. Only roles scoped to the whole tenant or to a team can be user-defined; the control plane reserves every other scope.

Roles TrueFoundry provides itself come in two flavours. Reserved roles (`is_editable = false`) cannot be managed at all and this resource refuses to adopt them. Default roles (`is_default = true`, e.g. `member`) can be updated in place, but they exist independently of Terraform — **import them, never create them**, and note that destroying one only removes it from state, leaving the control plane object with whatever permissions the last apply gave it.

Import an existing role by its name: `terraform import truefoundry_role.example member`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A custom tenant-scoped role granting read-only access to the AI gateway.
resource "truefoundry_role" "gateway_reader" {
  name          = "gateway-reader"
  display_name  = "Gateway Reader"
  description   = "Read provider accounts, models and MCP servers, use nothing."
  resource_type = "tenant"

  permissions = [
    "provider-account:ReadProviderAccount",
    "mcp-server:ReadMcpServer",
    "user:ListUsers",
  ]
}

# A team-scoped role. Team roles are assignable within a team rather than
# across the whole tenant.
resource "truefoundry_role" "team_gateway_user" {
  name          = "team-gateway-user"
  display_name  = "Team Gateway User"
  resource_type = "team"

  permissions = [
    "provider-account:UseIntegrations",
    "provider-integration:UseIntegration",
    "mcp-server:UseMcpServer",
  ]
}

# The `member` role every tenant ships with. TrueFoundry creates it at
# onboarding, so import it before the first apply — see import.sh — and note
# that `terraform destroy` only drops it from state, leaving the control plane
# role with the permissions of the last apply.
resource "truefoundry_role" "member" {
  name          = "member"
  display_name  = "Member"
  description   = "Role grants member access to the entities in the account."
  resource_type = "tenant"

  permissions = [
    "cluster:ReadCluster",
    "environment:ListEnvironments",
    "user:ListUsers",
    "team:ReadTeam",
    "provider-account:UseIntegrations",
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `display_name` (String) Human-readable name shown in the TrueFoundry UI.
- `name` (String) Name of the role (3-35 characters; must start with a lowercase letter, end with a letter or digit, and contain only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens), unique within the tenant. Changing it replaces the role.
- `permissions` (Set of String) Permissions the role grants, as `<entity>:<Action>` (e.g. `provider-account:UseIntegrations`). At least one is required. The accepted set is fixed by the control plane; if a control plane upgrade adds a permission this provider rejects, open an issue.
- `resource_type` (String) Scope of the role: `tenant` for a role assignable across the whole tenant, `team` for one assignable within a team. The control plane also accepts the legacy alias `account` and stores it as `tenant` — write `tenant`. Changing the scope of an existing role is rejected by the control plane; remove and re-add the resource instead of expecting an in-place change.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Human-readable description of what the role grants.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Control plane ID of the role.
- `is_default` (Boolean) True for roles TrueFoundry creates at tenant onboarding. Destroying such a role removes it from state only.
- `is_editable` (Boolean) False for roles TrueFoundry reserves; those cannot be managed or imported.
- `is_reserved` (Boolean) True for roles reserved by the control plane.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Roles are imported by their name.
terraform import truefoundry_role.gateway_reader gateway-reader

# TrueFoundry-provided default roles (is_default = true, e.g. `member`) exist
# before Terraform does. Import them rather than creating them, so the first
# plan shows the real diff against their current permissions.
terraform import truefoundry_role.member member

# Roles TrueFoundry reserves (is_editable = false, e.g. `tenant-admin` or
# `secret-group-viewer`) cannot be imported at all — reference them by name
# from a `role_id` attribute instead.
```
